name: Acid Reflux
description: Your basic attack becomes a lobbed shot with splash damage but deals 2 damage to you.
wikiEffects:
* Cats with Acid Reflux have their basic attack replaced with [[ability:Gerd Shot]].
** Gerd Shot overrides other ways of replacing basic attacks, such as [[ability:Paw Missile]] and [[item:Crown of Pestilence]].
wikiInteractions:
* [[ability:Careful]]: Protects allies from [[ability:Gerd Shot]] splash damage.
* [[ability:Split Shot]]: Increases [[ability:Gerd Shot]] area, at the cost of 50% less damage.

[[ability:Gerd Shot]] self damage does not scale, allowing cats to make consistent use of abilities that activate upon taking damage.
* [[ability:Bark Skin]]: The caster will only take 1 damage when casting Gerd Shot and gain an extra stack of [[status:Brace]] in the process.
* [[ability:Hulk Up]]: The caster gains +2 [[stat:SPD]] each time they cast Gerd Shot.
wikiObtaining:
* Possible outcome of events using the Physical Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the Stomach Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of a House event from a low Health stat.
wikiTrivia: * Ironically, though [[ability:Gerd Shot]] is granted by Acid Reflux, their real world counterparts behave the other way around, with Acid Reflux being a symptom of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD).

name: Acute Stress Reaction: Fight
description: -2 [[stat:SPD]] Gain +6 [[stat:STR]] while you have 5 or fewer HP.
wikiEffects:
* -2 [[stat:SPD]]
* +6 [[stat:STR]] while at 5 [[stat:HEALTH]] or less.
wikiInteractions:
* [[disorder:Scleroderma]]: +6 [[stat:STR]] is granted at the start of every battle.

* [[item:Nisshōki Bandana]]: Active at similar [[stat:HEALTH]] thresholds as cute Stress Reaction: Fight, while counteracting the afflicted cat's -2 [[stat:SPD]] with a [[status:Bonus Move]].
wikiTrivia:
* An Acute Stress Reaction is a psychological reaction to events that are terrifying, surprising or traumatic. The most common of these responses is known as the Fight-or-Flight Response, in which an animal will either "fight" or "flight" (flee) in response to an attack or threat to survival. Later research has shown there are a wide array of responses which can include, "fawn", "freeze", "flop", "faint", or "fright". 
** To match, there is a disorder named [[disorder:Acute Stress Reaction: Flight]] with the opposite effect of increasing [[stat:SPD]] at the cost of [[stat:STR]].

name: Addict
description: Start each battle with [[status:All Stats Down]]. Gain [[status:All Stats Up]] 3 whenever you eat a pill. You have a 50% chance to find a pill at the end of each battle.
wikiEffects:
* [[status:All Stats Down]] at the start of each battle.
* Using any of the following consumables grants [[status:All Stats Up]] for a net gain of 1:
** [[item:Bullseye]]
** [[item:Brain Candy]]
** [[item:Clover]]
** [[item:Disco Biscuit]]
** [[item:Percs]]
** [[item:Roid Rage]]
** [[item:Speedball]]
** [[item:Upper]]
** [[item:Witch's Eye]]

* One of these consumables also has a 50% chance to be added to the inventory at the end of every battle.
wikiInteractions:
* [[item:Mom's Ring]]: Guarantees an Addicted cat may negate given downsides every fight.
* [[ability:Scrapper]], [[item:Backpack]]: Addicted cats can repeatedly gain [[status:All Stats Up]] throughout the course of a single battle.
** [[ability:Vurp]]: Also works to this effect, but without the chance of producing additional pills.
* [[ability:Transcend]], [[ability:Cleanse]], [[ability:Shock Therapy]]: Removes [[status:All Stats Down]], allowing the first pill consumed to grant its full effect.

* Cats with a mutation or a mutation are unable to consume pills making this disorder a pure negative.
wikiObtaining:
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of a House event from a low Health stat.
wikiTrivia: * Addict's unused name is [[url:https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/pill_popper|Pill Poppers]], a slang for people addicted to illicit pills.

name: ADHD
description: +2 [[stat:SPD]], +1 [[stat:INT]]. You have 5 seconds to make decisions, or else this cat acts on its own.
wikiEffects:
* +2 [[stat:SPD]], +1 [[stat:INT]]
* The player has 5 seconds to make a decision for cats with ADHD; otherwise, the cat makes an AI-Controlled decision. The timer resets when a cat, either by player command or their own volition, moves, casts abilities or uses items.
wikiInteractions:
* [[ability:Waste Time]]: Mana Cost way to reset the 5 second timer.
* [[ability:MORE ANGRIER!!!]]: Fully depletes the cat's [[stat:MANA]], creating simpler turns where only one ability is used, somewhat alleviating the time limit constraint.

* [[disorder:Impostor Syndrome]]: Cats with ADHD will not trust suspicious cats, treating them as they would an enemy.

* [[item:Brain Chip]]: Overlaps with ADHD's downside, potentially making it more worthwhile to the wearer.
wikiObtaining:
* Possible outcome of events using the Mental Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Possible birth defect.
wikiTrivia:
* ADHD shares its "5-Second Rule" effect with [[item:Stopwatch]].
* [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attention_deficit_hyperactivity_disorder|Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder]] (ADHD) is a hereditary disorder in a person's executive (goal-oriented) functioning. Symptoms include inattention, impulsiveness (which may-or-may-not be paired with actual hyperactivity), and poor control of one's own emotions. It can also cause hyper-fixation, due to a weakened self-control.
wikiNotes: * Simply pausing the game will freeze the timer without penalty, allowing the player to give themselves more time to make decisions.

name: Albinism
description: Fire damage you take inflicts +3 [[status:Burn]]. Your basic attack has a 25% chance to inflict [[status:Fear]].
wikiEffects:
* Turns the cat's fur white regardless of their original color and their eyes gain a reddish tint.
* Any time a cat with Albinism receives el damage, they gain [[status:Burn]].
* The cat's basic attack has a 25% chance to inflict [[status:Fear]].
wikiInteractions:
* [[item:Water Feeder]]: Cleanses [[status:Burn]] at the start of the wearer's turn by applying [[status:Wet]] instead.
* [[ability:Pestilence]], [[item:Crown of Pestilence]]: Potential to mass-inflict [[status:Fear]], but might apply it to allies in the process.
** [[ability:Versatile Vocalist]]: Protects allies from being Feared.
wikiObtaining:
* Bad rare outcome of Event's [[stat:CHA]] skill check.
* Possible birth defect.
wikiTrivia: * Albinism is the congenital absence of melanin, resulting in pale white skin and reduced protection from UV Rays, hence the interaction with [[status:Burn]].

name: Anemia
description: When you take damage, you have a 10% chance to gain [[status:Bleed]] 1. Gain 2 Charge for each damage you take from [[status:Bleed]].
wikiEffects:
* Whenever an Anemic cat takes damage, they have a 10% chance to gain a stack of [[status:Bleed]]. 
** This includes damage from Status Effects, such as [[status:Bleed]] itself.

* Taking [[status:Bleed]] damage grants [[status:Charge]] for each point of damage taken.
wikiInteractions:
* a mutation : [[status:All Stats Up]] while [[status:Bleed]].
* [[ability:Sudden Affliction]]: The caster may give Anemic allies an additional burst of [[status:Charge]] before the end of a round.

Many items and mutations have ways of applying [[status:Bleed]] to a cat in order to lean into the risk-reward playstyle Anemia promotes.
* [[item:Broken Window]], [[item:Hybrid Hat]], a mutation: Anemic cats start each battle already Bleeding.
* [[item:Face Shards]]: Gain additional stacks of Bleed when damaged.
* [[item:Paw Shards]]: The wearer is able to control when they begin to Bleed each battle, as well as adding additional stacks manually.
* [[item:Bag o' Glass]], [[item:Bottles]], a mutation: Spawned [[obj:Glass]] may lead to higher stacks of Bleed.
wikiObtaining:
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of forbidden spells or items.
* Possible birth defect.
wikiTrivia: Anemia is a condition where one's blood has trouble carrying oxygen, whether due to a lack of red blood cells or other factors. Its association with prolonged bleeding in Mewgenics makes it easily confused with Haemophilia, another real-world disorder.
wikiNotes: * Anemic cats may be of great help in completing the [[item:Glass Cannon]] side quest due to the high amount of [[obj:Glass]] present in each battle, leading to near-guaranteed [[status:Bleed]].

name: Anxiety
description: +10% [[status:Dodge Chance]]. When you take damage, run away from the source.
wikiEffects:
* [[status:Dodge Chance]]
* When a cat with Anxiety takes damage, they will attempt to get as far away from the source as possible, similar to units affected by [[status:Fear]].
wikiInteractions:
* [[item:DNA Multiplier]]: Increases [[status:Dodge Chance]] granted by Anxiety.
Anxious cats can purposefully attempt to take damage in order to make use of items and abilities that take place during movement.
* [[ability:Mountain Form]]: Running away leads to more chances to spawn [[obj:Rock]].
* [[item:Spare Parts]]: Spawn additional Pickup when running away.
* [[item:Phoenix Hat]], [[item:Phoenix Mask]], [[item:Phoenix Necklace]]: Grant [[status:Charge]] each after running away.
wikiObtaining:
* Bad rare outcome of Event's all skill checks.
* Bad rare outcome of Event's [[stat:DEX]] skill check.
* Possible outcome of events using the Mental Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of a House event from a low Health stat.
wikiTrivia: * Despite its name, this disorder seems to reference generalized anxiety disorder rather than anxiety as an emotion. Generalized anxiety disorder is described as an anxiety disorder characterized by excessive, uncontrollable, and often irrational worry about events or activities (which gets translated as the +10% [[status:Dodge Chance]]).

name: Autism
description: +2 [[stat:INT]], -2 [[stat:CHA]] The abilities you were born with cost 2 less mana. Your other spells cost 1 more mana.
wikiEffects:
* +2 [[stat:INT]], -2 [[stat:CHA]]
* Active Abilities an Autistic cat is born with as a result of Breeding will have their costs reduced by 2 [[stat:MANA]]. This cost cannot be reduced below 1.

* All other spells gained by Autistic cats have their cost increased by 1 [[stat:MANA]]. This includes:
** Spells given by Class Collars at the start of a run.
** Spells acquired from Level Ups.
** Bonus Abilities.
** Abilities another spell replaces itself with, such as [[ability:Berserk]] with [[ability:Berserker Dash]].
*** This will be the case even if the cat with Autism was born with the initial spell.
wikiInteractions:
* [[ability:Brainstorm]]: Negates Autism's cost penalty after a single use.
* [[item:Two of Spades]]: Enables the double-casting of spells that would not otherwise meet the 1-2 Mana Cost requirement.
** This works both ways, as spells that usually cost 0 [[stat:MANA]] will now trigger Two of Spades. 
* [[ability:Braingeyser]], [[ability:Full Power]]: Autistic cats have an easier time reaching full [[stat:MANA]] due to their increased [[stat:INT]] and decreased [[stat:CHA]].
wikiObtaining: * Possible birth defect.
wikiTrivia:
* Autism, also known as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by differences or difficulties in social communication and interaction, a tendency to prefer predictability and/or routine, sensory processing differences, focused interests, and/or repetitive behaviors.
* The disorder's icon is a reference to the [[url:https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/tbh-autism-creature-yippee|Autism Creature]] (also known as TBH, or Yippee), humorously characterized as the mascot of autism.
wikiNotes:
* Autism may be slightly more detrimental to classes with multiple abilities that grant Supplementary Abilities, since these will always have their costs increased. For example:
** [[class:Fighter]] abilities such as [[ability:Throw Weapon (Bonus)]], [[ability:Slap]], and the previously mentioned [[ability:Berserker Dash]] will cost 1 [[stat:MANA]], potentially hindering their viability in low [[stat:INT]] builds. 
** [[class:Druid]] form-changing abilities such as [[ability:Form of the Elk]] will have their supplementary ability's cost increased.
** [[class:Tinkerer]] with [[ability:Mech Suit]], as each supplemenary ability will have its Mana Cost increased.

name: Bird Flu
description: Start each battle in Mockingbird Form. You have a 20% chance to recover at the end of each battle. Contagious.
wikiEffects:
* Cats with Bird Flu will cast [[ability:Form of the Mockingbird]] at the start of every fight; however, they do not gain [[ability:Tease]] after doing so. This effectively means that at the start of each fight, afflicted cats gain:
** [[status:Flying]]
** -2 [[stat:STR]], +2 [[stat:LCK]]
** [[ability:Mock Song]] as a replacement for their previous basic attack.
wikiInteractions:
* [[ability:Versatile Vocalist]]: As another [[class:Druid]] Ability, it pairs naturally with the granted [[ability:Mock Song]].
* [[ability:Magnify]], [[ability:Split Shot]]: Increases area of effect.
** [[ability:Split Shot]] is made purely beneficial, as [[ability:Mock Song]] does not deal damage to begin with.
* [[ability:Double Throw]]: Grants additional uses of [[ability:Mock Song]] without the usual downsides, as Mock Song deals no damage to begin with.
* [[status:Soul Link]]: The -1| [[stat:CON]] that comes with [[status:All Stats Down]], which [[ability:Mock Song]] applies twice, will be replicated as damage to all soul linked units.

* Abilities and items that replace a cat's basic attack such as [[ability:Spin to Win]] and [[item:Child's Skull]] will not override Bird Flu's effects as [[ability:Form of the Mockingbird]] is cast as a battle starts.
** Items and abilities such as [[ability:Form of the Wolf]] and [[item:Rotten Meat]] will override Mock Song as they can be used after the cat casts Form of the Mockingbird.
wikiObtaining:
* 50% chance to be applied to adjacent cats from a inflicted cat at the end of their movement action.
* Possible outcome of events using the Diseases pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of a House event from a low Health stat.
wikiTrivia: * Avian influenza or bird flu is a disease caused by the influenza A virus, which primarily affects birds but can be spread to humans.

wikiEffects:

wikiInteractions:
* [[ability:Flatline]], [[ability:Play Dead]], [[ability:Deep Dive]], [[ability:Seppuku]] or [[ability:Russian Shorthair Roulette]]: Allow for allies to down themselves manually, giving afflicted cats controllable mana refills.
*
wikiObtaining: * Good rare outcome of the Event's Sacrifice choice.
wikiTrivia:

** The South Park episode "Trapped in the Closet" states that disembodied thetans come from aliens who were cryogenically frozen, dropped into Earth's volcanoes, and subsequently nuked.

name: Blessing of Glorg
description: -2 [[stat:CON]] You can unequip cursed items.
wikiEffects:
* -2 [[stat:CON]]
* Items that cats with Blessing of Glorg have equipped with the [[status:Cursed]] keyword can now freely be unequipped, similar to the effect of [[item:Black Candle]].
wikiInteractions: * [[item:Callus]]: Can be unequipped and will keep its accumulated Shield for a new adventure.

* Glorg appears to be based on the "[[url:https://www.d20pfsrd.com/bestiary/monster-listings/templates/worm-that-walks-cr-2/|Worm that Walks]]", a monster created for the Call of Cthulhu tabletop game that was later brought to Pathfinder. This horrific entity is a swarm of decomposers (typically worms) following the will of the mind they've eaten, to the point of recreating its old body with their writhing mass.
** npc parodies this concept, fearing that the only reason he can move is because the Maggots in his body are playing along with his will.

name: Blood Frenzy
description: When you kill any unit, gain a Bonus Turn with [[status:Madness]].
wikiEffects:
* Whenever a frenzied cat downs or kills another unit, they immediately get an extra turn, during which they have [[status:Madness]].
** Extra turns can be granted by indirect actions such as [[status:Counter Attack]], knockback damage and Status Effects applied by the frenzied cat.
** Most effects that give cats extra turns have limits on their stacking, allowing the cat to obtain only one extra turn or not granting them on extra turns. After acquiring 10 extra turns on a round kills will no longer grant extra turns.
wikiInteractions:
* [[ability:Pestilence]], [[item:Crown of Pestilence]]: Especially deadly if there are multiple low-health enemies on the map. [[status:Madness]] afflicted cats are very likely to spam the spell version of Pestilence due to its low [[stat:MANA]] cost.

* [[disorder:Brave]], [[disorder:Soulless]], [[item:Tinfoil Hat]]: The frenzied cat is allowed full control during extra turns.

* [[ability:Butt Scoot]], [[ability:Leech Mother]],  [[item:Rotten Meat Mask]]: Weak Familiars make for easy ways of gaining extra turns.
** The frenzied cat is likely to hit the extra turn cap as they will be stuck in a loop of killing newly spawned adjacent familiars.
*** Though, this can be used to an advantage. If you can manage a stable mana income and the cat continuously spawns weak familiars and attacks them, said cat may be able to get more extra turns
** Unlimited use Weapons can help avoid this, especially ones that grant buffs such as [[item:Jitte]] or benefit from getting kills such as [[item:Gnarled Claw]].

* [[ability:Cryo-Heal]], [[ability:Frost Blast]], [[ability:Ice Surge]]: [[status:Freeze]] allies are protected from frenzied cats. [[status:Madness]] cats with Frost Blast or Ice Surge may use the spells on units before attacking, minimizing collateral damage.

* [[disorder:Dark One]]: Auto-casts a 1 damage spell that affects all tiles, this can inadvertently trigger it and the extra turns will auto-cast the spell.
* [[ability:Mini-Me]]: The AI-controlled copy of the frenzied cat will also be afflicted with [[status:Madness]] if it kills something.

* [[ability:Wrath of God]]: As long as it is not upgraded the cat will prioritize not hitting your allies when possible after they are downed, however it can still be very risky if the cats are spread out and have low body health.
* [[disorder:Pacifist]]: Makes all hits non-lethal, preventing this passive from triggering.
* [[ability:Order]] can easily manipulate a cat with blood frenzy to go near the enemies and have a huge chance to target enemies instead of your alies
wikiObtaining:
* Bad rare outcome of Event's [[stat:STR]] skill check.
* Very rare "Tragedy!" event.
** Edmund McMillen has confirmed that this way to get it is being rebalanced.
* Possible outcome of events using the Mental Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
wikiTrivia:
* Based on the Tragedy that applies it, Blood Frenzy may be a post-traumatic episode.
* Blood Frenzy may be named after "bloodlust" or "bloodthirst", the colloquial terms for homicidal ideation.
** Alternatively, since it triggers after killing, it might be an acute stress reaction.
wikiNotes:
* The [[status:Madness]] debuff makes the unit uncontrollable and has them regard all units as enemies. If a cat obtains Blood Frenzy while in a party, it is  recommended to not allow it to get final hits, as the cat will likely attack its allies.
** It is not recommended for a frenzied cat to apply damaging status effects on enemies, such as [[status:Bleed]], [[status:Burn]], or [[status:Poison]] while near allies. Enemies that die from a status effect will activate Blood Frenzy and cause the cat to get an extra turn immediately after.
** Positioning a frenzied cat near enemies and far away from allies can help mitigate risk, as they will target the closest unit.

* In a solo run, however, Blood Frenzy can potentially be very powerful, as it allows a cat to kill all enemies in one round, but careful planning is still recommended:
** Abilities that summon Familiars make for easy ways of gaining extra turns, though previously mentioned side effects and countermeasures should be taken into account.
** [[status:Madness]] cats have a tendency to disregard on-contact effects on their targets, such as [[status:Thorns]], [[status:Bleed Thorns]], [[status:Kinetic Spikes]] and [[status:Poisonous]] as well as forgetting if their targets might have [[status:Counter Attack]] or [[status:Backflip]].

* Familiars spawned while [[status:Madness]] are enemies, worsening the impact of Blood Frenzy.

* [[item:The Loner]] will not grant a frenzied cat extra turns unless they are ambushing the fight.
** This is because The Loner makes you kill your allies at Round 0 and then ends the round.
* Any unit can have only 10 turns per round.

name: Borrowed Time
description: +50% [[status:Dodge Chance]]. [[status:Doomed]] 3.
wikiEffects:

* [[status:Doomed]]

name: Brain Damage
description: You can't use item actions. +2 [[status:Brace]].
wikiEffects:
* [[status:Brace]]
* Cats with Brain Damage cannot use Trinkets, Consumables or Weapons during battle.
wikiInteractions:
* [[item:DNA Multiplier]]: Grants [[status:Brace]] instead.

Brain Damage is especially detrimental to classes that make frequent use of items in their Trinket and Weapon slots.
* [[class:Butcher]] can no longer use [[item:Meat Hook]].
* [[class:Tinkerer]] are no longer able to use weapons crafted when using [[ability:Craft Weapon]], limiting them to using [[ability:Throw Weapon]] to deal damage with them.
** Abilities such as [[ability:Fabricate]] and [[ability:Catbot]] that allow the Tinkerer to give crafted weapons to allies can greatly alleviate the downsides of Brain Damage.
* [[class:Monk]] are barred from using [[item:Stance Switcher]], locking them into Melee Stance unless an ability can force a switch, such as [[ability:Combo Throw]].
** Abilities that permanently switch the basic attack to something else such as [[ability:Form of the Wolf]] and [[ability:Spin to Win]] can circumvent this, as switching has limited use apart from triggering certain passives.
wikiObtaining:
Brain Damage occurs in a number of Disorder Pools:
* "General" Disorders
* Mental Disorders
* Physical Disorders

In [[chapter:The Core]], Brain Damage is the result of bad rare outcomes in a short event chain.
* At the Event, the cat must critically fail at the [[stat:LCK]] "Find another way around" skill check. This equips a [[item:Slag Tight]] onto the cat.
* In the follow-up event , the same cat must critically fail at the "Pull it out" option, which no stat can influence. This removes the [[item:Slag Tight]], but gives the cat Brain Damage and a permanent [[stat:INT]] penalty.
wikiTrivia: * The icon indicates that Brain Damage is specifically to the [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frontal_lobe|frontal lobe]]. This part of the brain controls dopamine flow to most of the rest of it, and thus plays an important role in executive (goal-oriented) functioning. People with frontal lobe damage typically struggle to bring themselves to do things, and may also react to things differently from beforehand.

name: Brain Dead
description: -10 [[stat:INT]], -5 [[stat:CHA]] Gain twice as many stats when you level up. +1 Reroll when leveling up.

wikiTrivia:
* Medically speaking, [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain_death|brain death]] is when the cerebral cortex is permanently destroyed, which is incompatible with higher brain function. A brain dead person is, effectively, not truly alive anymore, only their body lives on.
** Due to the fact that, in this context, brain death would have resulted in the cat dying, the trait is presumably referring to the cat just being a massive airhead.

name: Cancer
description: At the end of each battle, lose 3 random stats permanently and gain a random mutation.
wikiEffects:
* At the end of each battle, gain a Mutation, and permanently reduce three random Stats by 1, similar to the effect of [[item:Cancer]].
** The same stat may be chosen multiple times.
wikiInteractions:
* [[ability:Bare Minimum]]: Stat modifiers that would reduce any stat below 5 (or 7 when upgraded) are ignored.
** They don't go away, though; if Bare Minimum is replaced with another Passive, the cat's stats automatically update to reflect what they should be.
* [[item:Cat Rib]]: The reborn kitten will have all of Cancer's mutations without the stat penalties.
wikiObtaining:
* Bad rare outcome of Event's [[stat:STR]] skill check.
* Bad rare outcome of Event's [[stat:CON]] skill check.
* Bad rare outcome of Event's [[stat:CON]] and [[stat:STR]] skill checks.
* Bad common outcome of Event's Lick orb choice.
* 30% chance to be inflicted by a Cancer Cat's melee attack.
** If a Tiny Tumor summoned from [[item:Mother's Hat]], [[item:Mother's Necklace]] or [[item:Mother's Mask]] is [[status:Charmed]] or [[status:Madness]] into attacking a cat, it may also inflict Cancer.
* Possible outcome of events using the Diseases pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of a House event from a low Health stat.
wikiTrivia:
* [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancer|Cancer]] is a cell growth disorder, specifically one of uncontrolled cell growth from a part of a particular organ. An ordinary tumor is not a cancer until its cells "break out of" the body's broader structure, which leads to them "invading" other tissues and changing them to fit their own needs. Any cancer can eventually become lethal due to [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metastasis|metastasis]], which is when it spreads "secondary tumors" to other organs through the circulatory and/or lymphatic systems. Due to metastasis, few cancers have uniform symptoms, but most will eventually cripple one-or-more vital organs.
* Cancer is also a [[item:Cancer]]. This is a reference to the eponymous trinket from The Binding of Isaac, and the Disorder's icon is also a reference to that.

name: Dark One
description: At end of your turn, deal 1 damage to all units and heal for the damage dealt. Whenever you down an ally gain [[status:All Stats Up]].
wikiEffects: * Automatically casts a ability at the end of the cat's turn that damages all other units and heals the cat by 1 point per unit. Allies downed by this cat give it [[status:All Stats Up]]
wikiInteractions:
Dark One best pairs with items and abilities that summon large amounts of low health familiars.
* [[ability:Incubator]] : Spawns an allied Rot Fly for each unit hit when overhealed. These flies will later be killed for [[status:All Stats Up]] at the end of the cat's next turn.
* [[ability:Spoil]], [[ability:Lord of the Flies]] : All food pickups are converted into Rot Flies.
** [[ability:Butcher]] : Kills all units under 3 health and turns them into food pickups which can later be used with the aforementioned abilities.
* [[item:Caveman Wig]], [[item:Lice]] : The Lice spawned by these items are easily killed for [[status:All Stats Up]] at the end of the cat's turn.
Dark One also pairs well with abilities and items that can continuously down and revive allied cats.
* [[ability:Revive]], [[ability:Born Again]] : Mitigates the downside by allowing allied cats to continue fighting if they were inopportunely downed by Dark One.
** A cat that falls asleep after using [[ability:Born Again]] may be woken up early when damaged by Dark One's effect, potentially negating the downside.
* [[ability:Awaken]] : Allows the user to continually down their allies for [[status:All Stats Up]] stacks, with the caveat of massively injuring allied cats in the process.
** Abilities and items like [[ability:Go Limp]] and [[item:Bulletproof Vest]] can help prevent long-term damage to allied cats. Abilities that apply [[status:Zombie]], such as [[ability:Reanimate]], can also be used to this effect.
** [[item:Face Wrap]], [[item:Hockey Mask]], and other items with similar effects can be used to revive cats in place of abilities.

Dark One's primary downside comes from it being uncontrollable, often triggering a unwanted reaction to damage along with some passives.
* Stem Cat: Spawns Clot when damaged. Champion clots have enough health to tank a extra auto-cast, this can easily lead to a Dark One getting stuck in a stall loop when lacking high area damage.
* [[disorder:Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder]]: Inflicts [[status:Fear]] onto the cat but applies [[status:Damage Up]]

name: Deja Vu
description: 10% chance to cancel actions.   Deja Vu will go away when this cat returns to the house.
wikiEffects:
* A cat affected by Deja Vu has a 10% chance to cancel any action. This includes basic attacks, spells, weapons, and movement.

* If an active ability is cancelled, [[stat:MANA]] will still be spent.
* If a weapon, trinket or consumable is cancelled, uses will still be drained.
* If something with a (once per battle) restriction is cancelled, it will be count for the restriction.

* Unlike most other disorders, Deja Vu will be removed from an affected cat once an adventure ends.
wikiInteractions: * Cat can only have 2 disorders, so using abilities like [[ability:Forbidden Famine]] can remove Deja Vu.
wikiTrivia:
* Déjà vu is the phenomenon of feeling like one has lived through the present situation in the past. It's believed to be caused by the brain accidentally receiving the same signal twice.
* Déjà vu means already seen in French.

name: Depression
description: -1 [[stat:STR]], -1 [[stat:DEX]], -1 [[stat:CON]], -1 [[stat:INT]], -1 [[stat:SPD]], -1 [[stat:CHA]], -1 [[stat:LCK]] Adjacent units get [[status:All Stats Down]] 2.
wikiEffects:
* The cat starts every battle with [[status:All Stats Down]].
* Apply a temporary [[status:All Stats Down]] 2 to any adjacent unit.
wikiInteractions:
* [[ability:Grapple]]: Lock an adjacent unit in place to keep them debuffed.
** [[item:Twine Hat]], [[item:Twine Armor]], [[item:Twine Mask]], [[item:Hooked Necklace]]: Items that can be used to similar effect due to their ability to apply [[status:Grappled]].
wikiObtaining:
* Common bad outcome of Event's [[stat:CON]] skill check.
* Common bad outcome of Event's [[stat:STR]] skill check.
* Rare bad outcome of Event's [[stat:LCK]] skill check.
* Rare bad outcome of Event's ignore option.
* Possible outcome of events using the Mental Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of a House event from a low Health stat.
* Possible outcome of forbidden spells or items.
* Possible birth defect.
wikiTrivia: * Depression, or wikipedia, is a mood disorder characterized by long periods of apathy and sadness.
wikiNotes:
* The cat's own stat reductions are not permanent, and instead get expressed in each combat start as a debuff.
** Cleansing the cat's debuff each combat through any normal means, e.g. [[item:Enema]] or [[ability:Cleanse]], leaves only the adjacency debuffs with no downside to itself.
** This also means that the disorder does not affect [[stat:CHA]] directly nor its associated breeding chances in the house.
* The [[status:All Stats Down]] debuffs are removed from adjacent units after they leave to another tile, or when cleansed normally.
* Combat starts tend to favor grouping allies together, so the adjacency debuff is frequently applied for large parties.
* Prefer healing the cat with Depression at range as the adjacency debuff will impair any melee heals that scale off of a cat's stats.
** The most common form of healing, the [[class:Cleric]] [[ability:Melee Attack / Heal]] basic attack, is impaired by Depression (as it scales on [[stat:STR]]).
* For full-health units, moving adjacent to a cat with Depression practically means taking a non-lethal 8 damage. Lowering [[stat:CON]] by 2 reduces both max HP and thus HP by 8, but the rise in [[stat:CON]] after moving  away only increases max HP.
* Depression can be used offensively, functioning as a way to make nearby enemies weaker like a stronger [[item:The Tick]].

name: Diabetes
description: When you end your turn, if you haven't eaten food, gain [[status:All Stats Down]] and Confusion 1. Each time you eat food, cleanse all your debuffs and gain +1 [[stat:INT]].
wikiEffects:
* When the bearer ends their turn, if they haven't eaten food during that turn, they receive [[status:All Stats Down]] and [[status:Confusion]]. Whenever they do eat food, they cleanse all of their debuffs and gain [[status:Intelligence Up]].
** "Eating food" includes collecting [[obj:Food]] pickups and using certain consumable items.
wikiInteractions:
* [[class:Butcher]]: Butchers are designed around generating and consuming food pickups, meaning they are much more consistently able to eat and make use of the disorder's upside
** [[ability:Consume]] : Diabetes will immediately cleanse the [[status:Drowsy]] debuff, negating both downsides at once.
** [[ability:Regurge]] : Allows to consistently spawn a food pickup to trigger Diabetes upside and avoid it's downside.
** [[ability:Self Harm]] : Allows to consistently spawn a food pickup.

* a mutation/a mutation: Both of these mutations prevent the cat from eating food, which makes it impossible to activate the upside.
* [[disorder:Vegan]]: [[item:Big Bucket of Lard]] is the only way for a Vegan cat to trigger Diabetes.
wikiObtaining:
* Possible outcome of events using the Physical Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Possible birth defect.
wikiTrivia:
* [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diabetes|Diabetes]] is a collection of non-communicable diseases, each characterized by constantly-high blood sugar. The most common types have different causes; "type 1" is when the body doesn't make enough [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insulin|insulin]] for a normal person, while "type 2" is when the body needs far more insulin than a normal person.
* Interestingly, none of these items activate Diabetes:

** [[item:Dead Hummingbird]]
** [[item:Forbidden Fruit]]
** [[item:Gizzard]]
** [[item:Mushrooms]]
** [[item:Raptor Egg]]
wikiNotes:

Ebola has a high mortality rate in humans, but there is little evidence that suggests cats and other pets can spread Ebola, nor are the symptoms as severe .

wikiTrivia:
* In real life, [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigantism|Gigantism]] is caused by an excess of growth hormone in childhood, typically due to benign tumors on the [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pituitary_gland|pituitary gland]]. An adult more than 6 feet tall, or an adult man more than 6-and-a-half feet tall, is medically considered "gigantic". Technically speaking, Gigantism cannot develop after the body's longer bones fuse their "growth plates" shut, which stops them from lengthening. Once that happens, growth can no longer occur at a uniform scale, so anything that would cause Gigantism typically leads to [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acromegaly|acromegaly]] instead.

name: Kamikaze
description: You explode when you are downed.
wikiEffects:
When downed, this cat will explode, killing themselves in a Fire Explosion that:
* Hits a 3x3-tile area centered on this cat.
* Does 5 magic damage.
* Does not inflict [[status:Burn]], but will still impact tiles with the elements listed.
wikiInteractions:
Kamikaze is a very tough sell, since its upside (extra damage in a burst) pales in comparison to its downside (instant death on being downed). Some of its best "synergies" are with things that have overlapping downsides:
* [[item:Throbbing Gristle]], [[item:Steven's Gristle]], [[item:Party Detonator]]
Kamikaze can see limited use in abilities that summon copies of the cat, as summons will explode when dying and deal a small amount of damage to those around it.
* [[ability:Mini-Me]], [[ability:Summon Apprentice]], [[ability:Summon Shade]]
wikiObtaining:
Kamikaze is a Physical Disorder, and a "Forbidden Consequence" Disorder.

* Possible outcome of events using the Physical Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of forbidden spells or items.
wikiTrivia: * The Disorder's name and icon refer to the Kamikaze pilots of World War 2, who flew planes retrofitted to be cruise missiles in an effort to sink American warships. The icon art resembles the Japanese navy flag, which Kamikaze pilots allegedly wore on their bandanas.

name: Kidney Stone
description: When you end your turn take 1 damage and pass a kidney stone.
wikiEffects:
* When a cat with Kidney Stone ends its turn, it:
** takes 1 damage
** spawns a [[obj:Water]] directly behind itself
** spawns a [[obj:Small Rock]] behind itself, which is immediately knocked away from the cat, dealing 5 damage to any unit hit.
wikiInteractions:

** [[ability:Consume]] ([[class:Butcher]])
** [[ability:Yawn]] ([[class:Butcher]])

** [[ability:Think Deep]] ([[class:Psychic]])

* Anything that spontaneously ends the cat's turn, before it can choose which direction it's facing, can be very dangerous with [[disorder:Kidney Stone]]:

wikiTrivia:

name: Leprosy
description: [[status:Bruise]] 2. When you get hit, spawn a food pickup.
wikiEffects:
A Leper cat:
* Starts every battle with [[status:Bruise]].
* Drops a Pickup every time they take damage.
wikiInteractions:
* [[ability:Glutton]]: The Leper cat will immediately move to eat any Food pickups they drop, unless those pickups end up beneath other units. Cats with [[status:Trample]] will always attempt to move to the food, unless another cat eats it first.
* Some [[class:Cleric]] are able to treat Leprosy's downside, via [[ability:Cleanse]] or [[ability:Purifier]].
wikiObtaining:
* Possible outcome of events using the Diseases pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of a House event from a low Health stat.
wikiTrivia: * Leprosy is a specific bacterial infection that attacks one's nerves. It typically takes around five years for symptoms to manifest, and it is not very contagious. Aside from numbness, the nerve damage causes the body to lose awareness of its structural integrity; this leads to skin spots, muscle weakness, eye damage, and eventual deformation in the nose and face. Leprosy's association with "flesh falling off" is mostly due to indirect consequences, such as from the lack of pain in affected areas leading to additional (or more severe) injuries that get different infections.

name: Lycanthropy
description: 33% chance to enter Wolf Form at the start of your turn.
wikiEffects: * At the start of every turn the cat has a chance to automatically use [[ability:Form of the Wolf]] replacing the basic attack with [[ability:Wolf Claws]] and applying [[status:Intelligence Down]], [[status:Luck Down]], [[status:Strength Up]] [[status:Speed Up]], the cat however does not get [[ability:Pounce]]. A cat can transform multiple times per round.
wikiInteractions:
Lycanthropy best pairs with passives and mutations that would make use of multi-hit attacks such as those reliant on chance and status effects. Classes that otherwise use their basic attack for other purposes such as [[class:Necromancer]], [[class:Cleric]], and [[class:Tinkerer]] will suffer from having this disorder.
* [[class:Monk]] : Monk's basic attack has halved stat scaling, however [[ability:Wolf Claws]] hits twice and replaces it, while still retaining [[item:Monk Fist]]'s extra attack.
* [[ability:Razor Claws]] [[ability:Sharpen Claws]], : Inflicts [[status:Bleed]].
* a mutation : Applies a random debuff each hit.
* a mutation : 10% chance to Inflicts [[status:Bleed]] each hit.
* [[ability:Poison Tips]] : Inflicts [[status:Poison]].
* [[ability:Burning Paws]] : Inflicts [[status:Burn]].
* [[ability:Shiv]] : Increases critical chance, damage and inflicts [[status:Bleed]].
* [[ability:Dumb Muscle]] : Repeated transformations apply [[status:Intelligence Down]], making it easier to trigger its effect. When upgraded it gives a extra attack and move at -10 [[stat:INT]].
* [[ability:Cleanse]], [[ability:Transcend]] : Can remove the negative status effects applied when transforming.
* [[ability:Pray]] : Applies [[status:Luck Up]] and increases the chance of the cat transforming on their turn.
* [[item:Pack of Blades]], [[status:Serrated Claws]] : Backstabbing makes the basic attack apply [[status:Bleed]], the [[status:Speed Up]] helps with getting backstabs.
wikiObtaining:
* Possible outcome of events using the Diseases pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the Physical Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the Mental Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Can be inflicted by Half-Rat.
wikiTrivia:
* Lycanthropy is a mythological transformation into a werewolf. 
** Clinical lycanthropy is a psychiatric syndrome that involves a delusion that the affected person can transform into, has transformed into, or is a non-human animal.

name: Munchausen by Proxy
description: If you have a 2nd disorder, all other cats in your party gain it at the start of each battle.
wikiEffects:
By itself, [[disorder:Munchausen by Proxy]] does nothing.

If the cat with Munchausen's has a second Disorder, however, every other cat in the party has it as well.
* This shared Disorder does not take up one of the two Disorder slots.
* Disorders obtained mid-battle (such as from a Half-Rat) will not be shared until the next battle starts.
* It doesn't matter if one of the cats temporarily switches teams (due to [[status:Charmed]] or [[status:Possessed]]), since the Disorder is shared at the start of each battle.
wikiInteractions:
* [[disorder:Nudist]]: All cats gain +5 [[stat:SPD]] and 50% Dodge Chance, but can't equip any armor. 

* [[disorder:Chungus]]: Will give every cat +4 [[stat:CON]] with no downsides.
* [[disorder:Dark One]]: All cats will deal 1 damage to all units and heal for the damage dealt, outhealing the damage your cats will do to each other.

* [[disorder:Schrödinger's Syndrome]]: The player's chances of automatically losing a fight are low, but never zero. If every cat has 5 [[stat:LCK]], for example, the odds are 1-in-16.
* [[disorder:ADHD]]: Effectively imitates the [[item:Stopwatch]], except with a stat boost.
* [[disorder:Blessing of Glorg]]: You cannot unequip items mid-battle, leaving only the downside.
* [[ability:Schadenfreude]]: No effect from sharing a disorder with other cats. Possible bug.
wikiObtaining:
Munchausen By Proxy is a general Mental Disorder. It is not very easy to utilize, due to both its rarity and the fact that the cat needs another Disorder. The odds of a cat inheriting two Disorders in Breeding are a mere 2.25%, though some Birth Defect Disorders might be good to share.

* Possible outcome of events using the Mental Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
wikiTrivia:
* Munchausen by Proxy is internally referred to as skillshare_disorder as a counterpart to the [[ability:Skill Share]] passive.
* [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Factitious_disorder_imposed_on_another|Munchausen by Proxy]] (currently known as Factitious disorder imposed on another) is a mental health disorder in which a caregiver creates the appearance of health problems in another person.
* The Disorder being applied to all the other cats in the art is the art for [[disorder:Autism]].

name: Narcolepsy
description: At the end of your turn, fall asleep, heal 10 HP and gain 7 mana.
wikiEffects:
* At the end of the bearer's turn, they fall [[status:Sleep]], heal for 10 health, and gain 7 [[stat:MANA]].
** This effectively means the cat can only perform actions every other turn unless woken up.
wikiInteractions:
* [[item:Dream Catcher]]: Vastly improves the positive effects, as the cat will gain [[status:All Stats Up]], restore all [[stat:MANA]], and heal a random injury at the end of their turn.
* Extra turns given by abilities can be used to wake up from the [[status:Sleep]], allowing cats to act on the next turn properly.
** [[ability:Mind Meld]]
** [[ability:Chaos Rampage]]: The [[status:Madness]] and [[status:Confusion]] effectively have no effect, as the extra turn will be spent waking up from the [[status:Sleep]].
** [[disorder:Blood Frenzy]]: One blood frenzy turn can be used to skip the effects of sleep, with no downsides from the [[status:Madness]]. However, all following turns will take place as normal.
* [[ability:Purr]],[[ability:Cleanse]]: Debuff-removers in general can remove Narcolepsy's penalty. However, because Narcolepsy gives cats [[status:Sleep]] on turns when they're not asleep, this can be seen more like kicking the can.

* [[disorder:Sleep Paralysis]]: Any turn spent awake summons the Sleep Paralysis Demon at the end of the turn, causing the cat to sleep indefinitely.
wikiObtaining:
* Bad rare outcome from Event's [[stat:DEX]] skill check.
* Possible outcome of events using the Mental Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Possible birth defect.
wikiTrivia: * Narcolepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that impairs the ability to regulate sleep–wake cycles, and specifically impacts REM (rapid eye movement) sleep. The symptoms of narcolepsy include excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS), sleep-related hallucinations, sleep paralysis, disturbed nocturnal sleep (DNS), and cataplexy. People with narcolepsy typically have poor quality of sleep.

name: Necrophage
description: At the start of your turn, if there's a dead body near you, move towards it and eat it to gain [[status:All Stats Up]] and heal 4 HP.
wikiEffects:
* At the start of a turn if there is a corpse within the cat's movement range, it will automatically use its movement action to get adjacent to it and cast "Cannibalize" destroying it and gaining [[status:All Stats Up]] and Heal. a Necrophage can only auto-cast this once per turn.
** Necrophages will not use their movement action if they start their turn already adjacent to a corpse and will immediately auto-cast Cannibalize instead.
** Necrophages do not consider whether the corpse is a ally or enemy.
** [[status:Extra Moves]] and [[status:Bonus Move]]s will be expended to get close to corpses.
** Moving away from a [[disorder:Stinky]] cat takes priority over Necrophage.
wikiInteractions:

*

* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of a House event from a low Health stat.
wikiTrivia:
* Necrophages are animals that feed on decomposing dead animal biomass.
* This Disorder is similar to the native pathing of Zombie Cats.

name: Necrosis
description: +2 [[stat:STR]], +2 [[stat:CON]] When you take damage, you get -1 [[stat:CON]], -1 [[stat:STR]], and spawn poisoned food.
wikiEffects:
A Necrotic cat functions similarly to a Zombie Cat, without the [[status:Zombie]] tag and the corpse-eating:
* +2 [[stat:STR]], +2 [[stat:CON]]
* Whenever a Necrotic cat takes damage, they:

** Drop a [[obj:Poisoned Food]] pickup adjacent to themselves.

A Necrotic cat thus has a strong (or stronger-than-average) start at the beginning of a battle, but will get weaker and start to cause positioning problems as the battle progresses.
wikiInteractions:
* [[ability:Spoil]] can be used to turn poisoned food pickups spawned by Necrosis into Rot Fly familiars.
* [[ability:Cleanse]] treats the stat debuffs and purifies the poisoned food in its area-of-effect.

* Bad rare outcome of Event's [[stat:DEX]] skill check.
* Bad rare outcome of Event's skill checks.

wikiTrivia: * Necrosis is a medical term that refers to the premature death of cells and buildup of decomposing material within organic tissue.

description: +5 [[stat:SPD]] +50% [[status:Dodge Chance]]. You can't wear armor.

name: Obsessive Compulsive Disorder
description: Bonus Ability: Groom At the end of your turn, if you didn't use Groom, take 2 damage.
wikiEffects:
A cat with OCD starts each battle with [[ability:Groom]] as a Bonus ability.
* Groom is a ActiveType ActiveType (listed as just a heal due to its lack of damage) that Mana Cost.
* It can be used on the user, or on units within melee Reach.
* It cleanses the target of all Debuffs on them, except for permanent ones.

If a cat with OCD doesn't use [[ability:Groom]] during their turn, it takes 2 damage at the end of it.
wikiInteractions:
* [[ability:Copycat]]: If another cat has Copycat, they can make use of Groom as well, or even Groom+ (which also does Heal) if Copycat is upgraded.
* [[ability:Exert]]: Groom removes the [[status:Drowsy]] penalty from using this ability.
* [[ability:Bare Minimum]]: Ensures the cat has enough [[stat:INT]] to at least use Groom once per turn.
* [[disorder:Leprosy]], [[disorder:Necrosis]], [[disorder:Borrowed Time]]: Knowing Groom lets a cat with OCD manage their Debuffing downsides quite effectively.
* [[disorder:Anemia]]: Knowing Groom lets an Anemic cat control their [[status:Bleed]], by ending it before it gets lethal. 3 Bleed damage pays for a single use of Groom.
* [[disorder:Blood Frenzy]]: A [[status:Madness]] cat may Groom themselves, if they have Mana left over after nuking everyone around them, yanking themselves out of Madness (until their next extra turn).
wikiObtaining:
* Possible outcome of events using the Mental Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of a House event from a low Health stat.
* Possible birth defect.

name: Orange Fetin
description: You have a 10% to be AI controlled each turn. When you kill an enemy, gain 3 mana and heal 2 hp.
wikiEffects:
* After killing an enemy: gain 3 mana and heal 2 HP.
* 10% chance (at 5 luck) to be AI-controlled each turn. AI-controlled cats...
** Will avoid ending their turn, potentially spending mana on unhelpful spells or using consumables prematurely.
** May target [[status:Freeze]] or otherwise impervious units.
** Disregard on-contact effects on their targets, such as [[status:Thorns]], [[status:Bleed Thorns]], [[status:Kinetic Spikes]] and [[status:Poisonous]].
** Disregard effects such as [[status:Counter Attack]] or [[status:Backflip]].
** May attack and destroy familars or downed allies if it gets them closer to enemies.
wikiTrivia:
* Each Fetin may be a reference to the [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thetan|thetan]], the concept of the soul in Scientology. 
** Scientologists believe that most people contain disembodied thetans, which may influence their behavior and give them memories of past lives.
** The South Park episode "[[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trapped_in_the_Closet_(South_Park)|Trapped in the Closet]]" states that disembodied thetans come from aliens who were cryogenically frozen, dropped into Earth's volcanoes, and subsequently nuked.

name: Osteogenesis Imperfecta
description: +2 [[status:Bruise]], +2 [[status:Bleed Thorns]], and +2 [[status:Thorns]]. When you're downed, you get injured an extra time.
wikiEffects:
* The afflicted cat begins each battle with +2 [[status:Bruise]], +2 [[status:Bleed Thorns]], and +2 [[status:Thorns]].
* Additionally, each time they are downed, they recieve an additional [[status:Random Injury]].
wikiInteractions:
* [[ability:Thick Skull]]: The double injuries will speed up the rate at which the cat gains Concussions.
* [[ability:My Leg!]]:  The cat will only need to be downed twice for this passive to reach its own potential, on top of the amount of [[status:Thorns]] the cat would gain.
* [[item:Bulletproof Vest]]: Blocks the double injuries the cat would receive.
wikiObtaining:
* Possible outcome of events using the Physical Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Possible birth defect.
wikiTrivia: * Osteogenesis imperfecta, also known as brittle bone disease, is a group of genetic disorders that all result in bones that break easily.

name: Pacifist
description: You can't kill units. If you end your turn without using your basic attack gain 7 mana.
wikiEffects:
* A cat with this disorder cannot kill other units. 
** They can still deal damage to other units, however any and all damage that would be lethal leaves the unit on exactly 1 HP.
* If a cat with Pacifist ends their turn without using their basic attack, they receive 7 [[stat:MANA]].
wikiInteractions:
* More supportive classes like [[class:Druid]], [[class:Cleric]], certain [[class:Psychic]] builds, etc. are not as heavily impacted by the downside, and may even benefit from the bonus mana gain.
** [[class:Druid]]'s crow familiar will be unable to kill enemies, however.
* [[ability:Zenkai Boost]]/[[ability:Death's Door]]: Pacifist cats could deliberately attack allies with these passives to trigger their activation conditions.
wikiTrivia: * Pacifism is a philosophy that entails opposition to war and/or violence, and is a common tenet of several religions such as Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism.

name: Paranoia
description: When a unit ends its movement directly behind you, attack it and gain [[status:Fear]].
wikiEffects:
* Any unit that ends their movement behind this cat will be attacked by the cat, and the cat will gain [[status:Fear]].
** The cat will turn towards the unit behind them, attack, stay facing the unit, then gains [[status:Fear]].
* This effect counts for allies, as well as objects such as [[obj:Rock]] and [[obj:Poop]].
wikiInteractions:
* [[disorder:Brave]] will remove the [[status:Fear]] gained after triggering this disorder.
* Items that grant [[status:Holy Shield]] can be helpful in preventing the initial damage caused by unlucky spawn formations.
* The [[class:Cleric]]'s [[ability:Cleanse]] ability can be useful to purge the [[status:Fear]] status effect before the afflicted cat wastes its movement action running away during its upcoming turn.
* The [[class:Tank]]'s [[ability:Hard Head]] passive allows the cat to consistently block melee attackers, as enemies prioritize backstabs and this disorder causes cats to immediately face those that end their movement behind them.
** Alternatively, granting knockback to the cat will give similar results as the attacker will always get pushed away before they can even perform their attacks.
wikiTrivia: * Paranoia is the belief that everything is about the person who is experiencing the paranoia. Making false accusations and carrying a general distrust of other people also frequently accompany paranoia.
wikiNotes:
* Many battles have starting formations that place player cats behind each other, causing this disorder's effects to trigger immediately after the battle starts.
** This can lead to friendly casualties depending on the afflicted cat's attack strength and the unlucky ally's health.

name: Paraplegic
description: +2 [[stat:INT]] The range of all your movement, dash, and jump abilities are capped at 1 unless they teleport. Enemies won't prioritize attacking you.
wikiInteractions:
* [[ability:Overflow]]: The upgraded version Gives teleport as a movement action while at full Mana.
* [[ability:Take Aim]] works as a decent synergy due to bonuses relating to not moving.
wikiTrivia:
* [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraplegia|Paraplegia]] is a condition often caused by spinal cord injuries or birth defects, and results in loss of motor control and/or feeling in the lower body.
* The image for Paraplegia is the [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Symbol_of_Access|International Symbol of Access]], depicting a person in a wheelchair. This symbol represents that something has been added to assist the disabled, such as reserved parking spots or door opener buttons.
** This ties in with the Disorder, as paraplegic people are restricted to a wheelchair due to the inability to use their legs.
* "Enemies won't prioritize attacking you" plays off the belief that attacking handicapped individuals goes against ethical standards.

name: Phony
description: +2 [[stat:CHA]] Start each battle with full mana. You can't regenerate mana.
wikiEffects:
[[disorder:Phony]] is an unusual Disorder, in that it effectively disables one of the bearer's seven Stats. A "Phony" cat:
* has +2 [[stat:CHA]].
* starts each battle with full (maximum) [[stat:MANA]].
* starts each battle with [[status:No Mana Regen]], preventing their [[stat:INT]] from regenerating spent Mana.

The cat's [[stat:INT]] is not actually zeroed out, and will still affect abilities such as [[ability:Paw Missile]] and [[ability:Energy Blast]]. It will also function in Events.

Still, a "Phony" cat will have to make the most of a single Mana bar's worth of Mana, for an entire fight. This Disorder can be a great boon for cats with powerful Active Abilities, and a headache for cats with slowly-ramping ones (i.e. [[ability:Ice Surge]]). The longer a fight drags on, the more problems a "Phony" cat will run into; provided they rely on spells for their damage.
wikiInteractions:
Phony best pairs with passives and equipment that increase [[stat:CHA]] and high damage abilities that are normally limited by their high Mana Cost.
* [[ability:Hunter's Boon]]: Allows a Phony to replenish (and/or top off) their Mana through violence.
* Debuff Removers i.e [[ability:Cleanse]], [[item:Cat o' Nine Tails]] : Can remove [[status:No Mana Regen]].
* [[disorder:GIGACHAD]]/[[disorder:Down's Syndrome]]/[[disorder:Williams Syndrome]]: Increased [[stat:CHA]] stacks very well with Phony's upside, while decreased [[stat:INT]] largely overlaps with its downside.
* [[item:Bag of Grass]]: Any Mana-restorer will be extra useful for a Phony, at least in fights where a single full Mana bar is insufficient; the Bag of Grass simply stands out for its multiple uses.
* [[item:Dunce Cap]]: Allows a Phony to cast more spells while ignoring the downside of the item.
*  [[obj:Flower]] and [[obj:Tall Flower]] will still give its mana regeneration effect to Phony cats despite the debuff. Skills and items that generate those tiles like [[item:Flower Mix]] may help in long-term fights.
* [[class:Psychic]] has several abilities that complement this disorder:
** [[ability:Gravity Blast]]: deals +10 Knockback Damage when cast at full Mana
** [[ability:Increase Gravity]]: deals 6 damage and inflicts [[status:Stun]] at full Mana
** [[ability:Think Deep]]: Refills the Mana bar (but also puts the user to [[status:Sleep]])
** [[ability:Enlightened]]: Gives the Phony [[status:Free Spell]] each turn at full Mana
** [[ability:Full Power]]: Triples the Phony's basic attack damage, and gives it +3 Knockback, at full Mana
** [[ability:Mad Visage]]: The Phony's basic attack inflicts [[status:Madness]] at full Mana
** [[ability:Overflow]]: The Phony [[status:Flying]] and has [[status:Brace]] at full Mana, though the floating Mana cap will be largely unused
* [[ability:Latent Energy]]: While it has negligible effect unless upgraded on the Phony cat itself, having a full bar of mana allows a different cat with Latent Energy to stack [[status:Magic Damage Up]] boosts.
* [[class:Fighter]] also has abilities that complement this disorder as [[stat:INT]] is no longer necessary:
** [[ability:Stoopzerk]] has no downside due to Phony already preventing mana regen.
*** [[ability:MORE ANGRIER!!!]] can be cast with a much higher Mana amount than usual, allowing for a much higher [[stat:STR]] increase.
** [[ability:Think Too Hard]] allows for more high-mana spells to be cast.
** [[ability:Dumb Muscle]] increases [[stat:STR]] and critical hit chance, and grants a second move and attack per turn if upgraded.
** [[ability:Thick Skull]] causes all injuries to be Concussions, which have no downside.
* [[item:Soul Jar]]: Due to the cat only lasting 1 turn, the lack of mana regen is not an issue.

* [[ability:Braingeyser]]: Won't come into play without external Mana gain.
* [[ability:Power Up]]: Won't come into play without external Mana gain.
* [[ability:Epiphany]]: All mana will be lost after the cat's first turn, and the upside has no effect.
wikiObtaining:
Phony is a Mental Disorder.
* Possible outcome of events using the Mental Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
wikiTrivia:
* Phony is a [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nominalized_adjective|nominalized adjective]], synonymous with "fraud" when used as a noun (or with "fake" when referring to an object).
* One of Phony's definitions is imitating something superior; which is reflected in its gameplay, as a Phony Cat can use multiple spells right away but is unable to replicate that power again.
* Phony's effect has the cat's [[stat:MANA]] behave like how it would work in traditional role-playing games, ranging from Dungeons & Dragons to Final Fantasy.

name: Pica
description: When you collect a coin or scrap pickup, heal instead of gaining the pickup's normal effect.
wikiEffects:
* Collecting any non-[[obj:Food]] pickup will heal the bearer instead of giving its normal effects. The healing received depends on the quality of the pickup as follows: 
** [[obj:Coin]] 
*** +3 Heal (Every additional coin on the tile will increase the heal by 3. Up to +30 Heal for a stack of 10 coins.) 
** [[obj:Scrap]] 
*** Small  +4 Heal
*** Large  +12 Heal
wikiInteractions:

name: Psychosis
description: +1 [[stat:STR]], +1 [[stat:DEX]], +1 [[stat:CON]], +1 [[stat:INT]], +1 [[stat:SPD]], +1 [[stat:CHA]], +1 [[stat:LCK]] Gain [[status:Madness]] for the rest of the battle after this unit ends their first turn.
wikiEffects:
Psychosis an extremely dangerous Disorder. A Psychotic cat:
* Has +1 to each of their seven main Stats.
* Has only one turn of lucidity each battle; afterwards, they are [[status:Madness]] until the battle ends.
** If Psychosis is gained during a battle, they immediately go Mad, even if it's still their first turn.
** This is a permanent version of the status effect; removing it will not work, because it will reapply itself.
** Immunity to [[status:Madness]] will prevent the status effect from applying.
wikiInteractions:
* [[disorder:Brave]], [[item:Tinfoil Hat]], [[disorder:Soulless]]: Prevents the cat from actually getting Madness.

* [[item:Cursed Stickman]]: The two typically come together, due to the "Ominous" event. The Item has a 10% chance to give the Psychotic bearer Madness on their first turn (as well).
* [[disorder:Sociopathy]]: Effectively permanent madness if your cat does not have a way to prevent it
wikiObtaining:

* Possible result from Event's bad rare outcome with the [[stat:CON]] skill check.
* Having the [[item:Happy Helmet]] break when equipped.

* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
* Possible outcome of forbidden spells or items.
wikiTrivia: * Psychosis is the inability to distinguish what is or is not real. Symptoms include delusions, hallucinations, and disorganized or incoherent thoughts or speech.
wikiNotes:
Psychosis is not an insurmountable challenge for a party to bear, but it poses a bunch of problems in battle. Being AI-controlled in general is not ideal, since the AI tends to burn all of its [[stat:MANA]] on ActiveType. Aside from that, several enemies and Bosses have special reactions to certain attacks or moves. [[status:Madness]] is worse than normal AI-controlled hijinks (such as [[disorder:Severe Deja Vu]]) because a Mad cat will consider itself "neutral" -- or, in other words, against everyone.

A Psychotic cat has a few perks over a vanilla cat. The first is that, while [[status:Madness]], they ignore "once-per-battle" restrictions; this lets them spam Forbidden spells, for example, which might have them replace their Psychosis with something less toxic (such as [[disorder:Anemia]] or [[disorder:Necrosis]]). The second is the full-spectrum stat boost, which is nice for Events.

name: Rabies
description: Your basic attack is a melee attack. You can't equip face armor. After each battle, gain +2 [[stat:STR]] and -1 [[stat:INT]]. If your [[stat:INT]] is 0 or less, you have [[status:Madness]].
wikiEffects:
* Replaces the basic attack with [[ability:Melee Attack (Collarless)]].
* At the end of each battle, gain +2 [[stat:STR]] and lose -1 [[stat:INT]].
* If the cat's [[stat:INT]] is ever 0 or less, gain the [[status:Madness]] condition, and attack the closest unit on your turn.
* Cats with this disorder are unable to equip face armor.

Without a reliable way to raise intelligence, it is possible for a cat with Rabies to quickly become stuck with the [[status:Madness]] condition. Items such as [[item:Tinfoil Hat]] can negate the effects of Madness, but will not negate intelligence loss caused by this disorder.
wikiInteractions:
* [[class:Monk]] : Monk's basic attack has halved stat scaling, however [[ability:Melee Attack (Collarless)]] has full [[stat:STR]] scaling and replaces it, while still retaining [[item:Monk Fist]]'s extra attack. Monk's +2 [[stat:INT]] also means it will last more fights without getting [[status:Madness]].
* [[ability:Bare Minimum]] : can allow a cat to get the benefit of this disorder without the drawback. This also ensures they don't get [[status:Madness]].
* [[item:Libra]] : Results in a net positive stat gain, ensuring that the cat never falls to [[status:Madness]].
* [[item:Tinfoil Hat]] : Prevents [[status:Madness]] without correcting [[stat:INT]], in case the player wishes to use [[ability:Think Too Hard]] or [[ability:Dumb Muscle]].
wikiObtaining:
Rabies is a Disease, though not one that shows up at the House from poor Health.

* 25% chance to be applied from a inflicted cat's basic melee attack.
* Rare bad outcome of Event's [[stat:CON]] and [[stat:DEX]] skill checks.
* Possible outcome of events using the Diseases pool.
* Possible outcome of events using the General Disorders pool.
wikiStrategy:
Rabies is most effective on cats that can benefit from long-term battle scaling without relying heavily on Intelligence. Because the disorder grants +2 [[stat:STR]] and removes -1 [[stat:INT]] after every battle, its offensive value increases over time while gradually reducing the unit's decision reliability.

Once Intelligence reaches 0 [[stat:INT]] or lower, the cat gains [[status:Madness]], causing it to attack the nearest unit on its turn. This makes Rabies increasingly risky in longer runs unless the player has a plan to mitigate the effects of Madness or compensate for low-Intelligence behavior.

Effects such as [[ability:Bare Minimum]] are particularly valuable because they preserve the Strength scaling while preventing the downside associated with Madness, allowing the disorder to function as a long-term damage amplifier.
wikiTrivia: * Rabies is a brain-invasive disease known for causing violent excitement and confusion, as well as rapid deterioration of cognitive function. This is represented through the disorder's effect in which a cat gains strength and loses intelligence until it gains the madness condition, attacking all units near it.

wikiInteractions:

* [[item:Two of Spades]]: Double cast all spells.

* [[ability:Zenkai Boost]]: Grants random permanent stat point/s and starts next battle with [[status:All Stats Up]] if the disordered cat is not downed at the end of battle.
* [[ability:Overflow]]: Starts battle with 1 mana in most cases, but uncaps your mana, allowing end-of-turn mana gain and other mana gain effects to work unrestricted, and nearly constant uptime on the passive's effects at full mana.

name: Williams Syndrome
description: -5 [[stat:INT]], +10 [[stat:CHA]] Your attacks may [[status:Charmed]].
wikiEffects:
Cats with Williams Syndrome have -5 [[stat:INT]] and +10 [[stat:CHA]]. In addition, their attacks have a chance to inflict 1 [[status:Charmed]].

The extra starting [[stat:MANA]] from a high Charisma can be useful to a wide array of cats. However, the low Mana regeneration from a low Intelligence can harm cats who rely on Mana for most of their damage output. This is more relevant in extended fights, such as against Bosses.

The Charm chance is more role-defining. Williams Syndrome gives the basic actions of [[class:Cleric]] and [[class:Druid]] a chance to "backfire", by making allies AI controlled for a turn.
wikiInteractions:
* [[ability:1D Chess]]: The lowered Intelligence provides higher amounts of movement.
* [[ability:Dumb Muscle]]: The lowered Intelligence makes it easier for cats to activate the bonuses.
* [[ability:Think Too Hard]]: The Intelligence penalty reduces this ability's self-damage, potentially to zero, while the Charisma bonus lets the user use this more often.
* [[ability:Math?]]: Since all active abilities will cost 3 Mana, Williams Syndrome guarantees you can use at least 3 more abilities than without it.
* [[item:Libra]]: As the sum of the stat changes is positive (+5), it only grants positive stats with Libra.
* [[ability:Invert]]: Cats with this disorder will usually have their highest stat be [[stat:CHA]] and their lowest be [[stat:INT]], which [[ability:Invert]] reverses. A cat with very low or negative [[stat:CHA]] after inverting may not be able to reap the benefit of high [[stat:INT]], however.
** However, the Psychic has several abilities which reward a high Intelligence, low Charisma playstyle, meaning Invert is better for Psychics with Williams Syndrome.
* [[disorder:Phony]]: Triples the mana of the cat at the start of the battle. If the cat's Intelligence is low enough, Phony has no downside.
wikiObtaining: * Possible birth defect.
wikiTrivia: * William's Syndrome or Williams-Beuren syndrome, is a genetic disorder caused by missing specific genes of the 27th chromosome. People with Williams-Beuren syndrome exhibit a lower IQ, especially in regards to visual-spatial learning disabilities. However, they exhibit impressive social and verbal abilities relative to their cognitive deficits, and are known for being charming, kind and social.
